items.title: Why AI’s easiest wins are misleading CEOs
AI is changing work. Now it has to change the organization
items.desc: The first phase of enterprise AI put powerful new tools in people’s hands. Capturing the larger opportunity from agentic AI will require leaders to rethink the shape of the organization itself.

items.title: Scaling AI inference
items.desc: Inference is reshaping AI economics, infrastructure architectures, and investment priorities across the semiconductor ecosystem.

items.title: Pause, pivot, or accelerate: SaaS in the age of agentic AI
items.desc: Agentic AI is reshaping the case for modernization in insurance. Leaders from Guidewire, Bessemer Venture Partners, and SAP discuss how insurers can respond, considering their existing commitments.

items.title: Siemens’s next reinvention: An interview with Cedrik Neike
items.desc: As technology transforms the factory floor, industrial companies are confronting a broader question: What will it take to lead the next era of manufacturing?

items.title: The bank’s digital twin: The future of nonfinancial risk management
items.desc: The risk function’s fundamental purpose has not changed, but the nature of the risks, the pace at which they materialize, and the tools available to manage them have.

items.title: Modernizing for the mission: An interview with Jamie Wolff
items.desc: The National Nuclear Security Administration’s CIO shares that modernization means rebuilding infrastructure, data, and talent at once—while keeping the mission and a relentless pace of change in mind.

items.title: The CEO’s singular impact on the success—or failure—of AI in organizations
items.desc: There are certain aspects of the AI opportunity that chief executives cannot hand off to others—raising the organization’s ambition, rearchitecting how it works, and resetting its culture.

items.title: Workforce in motion: Skills and pathways to future jobs in the United States
items.desc: AI, automation, and broader structural trends are accelerating the reallocation of work across the US economy. Capturing its benefits requires developing new professional pathways and skills, and reducing barriers between declining and growing occupations.

items.title: The next phase of government AI economics
items.desc: Subsidized AI pilots are expiring as usage explodes. Here’s how US public sector leaders can treat AI spend as a managed category before the bill arrives.

items.title: Make life better: Mikhail Lomtadze’s customer-first philosophy
items.desc: Mikhail Lomtadze, cofounder and CEO of Kaspi, believes the only measure that matters is whether Kaspi makes customers’ lives better or not—and why that single conviction changes everything else.

items.title: AI is changing how we work. Is your organization ready?
items.desc: As AI reshapes roles, leaders face a bigger question: how to rethink jobs, teams, and the way work gets done in a fundamentally different era.

items.title: The AI-powered future of care
items.desc: AI won’t replace clinicians, but it can improve quality, increase access, and reshape the workforce, payments, and patient volumes. Today, AI can perform some 16 to 22 percent of US outpatient care.

items.title: Democratized superintelligence is coming: The world needs to get ready
items.desc: Bret Taylor, Sierra cofounder and OpenAI chair, believes AI’s near-term cybersecurity risks are real but solvable, and its greater power lies in delivering the world’s best knowledge to everyone.

items.title: Harnessing AI to make mining safer
items.desc: AI could improve both safety and productivity by anticipating problems before they arise, detecting worker fatigue, and automating dangerous tasks.

items.title: Maintenance meets AI: A proven approach for asset-heavy industries
items.desc: Embedding the latest AI and technology within day-to-day operations is transforming maintenance from a cost center into a significant driver of value.

items.title: India’s new insurance track: The marathon becomes an AI-led decathlon
items.desc: As India’s economy continues to ramp up, insurers have an opportunity to capture value by improving productivity, modernizing operating models, and scaling technology and AI across the enterprise.

items.title: Rewiring procurement in resources: Making judgment an enduring asset
items.desc: For procurement leaders in the resources sector, using AI to codify the function’s category expertise does not just capture more value—it turns hard-won judgment into a compounded, durable advantage.

items.title: Ready to ramp? How US manufacturers can scale at pace
items.desc: US manufacturers have a once-in-a-generation opportunity to reshore the production of critical and at-risk goods, but to do so, they will need to aggressively ramp up production from today’s levels.

items.title: WIRED: The AI playbook top companies use
items.desc: WIRED’s Katie Drummond talks with McKinsey’s Dan Swan about why capturing AI’s full potential requires companies to move beyond experimentation and fundamentally rewire their businesses.

items.title: The economics of AI
items.desc: AI is getting more expensive for companies. As rising token usage and workflow complexity make costs harder to predict, leaders need new ways to manage AI economics.

items.title: AI drug discovery: Focusing on what matters most
items.desc: AI is accelerating drug discovery, but investment has concentrated in molecule design—the stage with the best data and clearest tools. The industry’s real constraint lies elsewhere: identifying and validating the right disease mechanism.

items.title: Novartis’s Christian Diehl on scaling AI beyond the demo
items.desc: Novartis’s chief data and digital officer for biomedical research explains how data platform investments are paying off in AI safety prediction, generative chemistry, and faster translation.

items.title: The $2.3 trillion horizon: How AI is rewriting the semiconductor story
items.desc: AI is fueling unprecedented semiconductor growth while upending long-standing industry dynamics and shifting the sources of value.

items.title: Cutting the ‘coordination tax’: How agentic AI can reshape workflows
items.desc: Organizations must redesign workflows to realize value from AI, but the challenge is where to begin. An opportunity lies between workflow steps, where work passes between teams and systems.

items.title: Europe’s new AI edge? The emerging application layer opportunity
items.desc: As enterprises shift from experimenting with models to redesigning workflows, new research suggests Europe could be well-positioned for this new AI application era.

items.title: State of Consumer Africa 2026: Meeting the pragmatic shopper
items.desc: Household budgets in Africa are tight and channels increasingly fragmented. Four trends are redefining how consumers discover, decide, and spend, and how consumer-facing companies can respond.

items.title: How leaders are turning AI into growth
items.desc: Nearly 90 percent of companies are investing in AI, but only 6 percent see material impact. The difference is in how they approach it.

items.title: LATAM’s reinvention at 35,000 feet
items.desc: Partnering with McKinsey, the airline rewired its organization to make digital and AI core parts of the business—transforming the passenger experience, accelerating growth, and unlocking new levels of operations performance.

items.title: Navigating the new normal: Building resilience in fuel retail trading
items.desc: Commodity markets have entered a new era of persistent volatility. For fuel retailers, this is a chance to strengthen resilience and unlock value, but only with strategic investment and a shift in mindset.

items.title: Convenience or discovery: Which mission will your store serve?
items.desc: As AI reshapes how consumers browse, shop, and buy, retailers must choose a mission for every location—and commit to it.

items.title: Billion-dollar beauty: The odds of scaling a breakout brand
items.desc: Our new analysis reveals the odds of reaching $1 billion in sales—and how the paths to that milestone differ by category and ownership.

items.title: The new growth mandate: A conversation with LinkedIn CMO Jessica Jensen
items.desc: At Cannes Lions 2026, LinkedIn CMO Jessica Jensen and McKinsey senior partner Dianne Esber discussed what it takes to turn AI from experimentation into a catalyst for growth.

items.title: Author Talks: The business of owning a sports team
items.desc: How does business ownership compare with owning a sports team? Baltimore Orioles owner David M. Rubenstein explains the leadership mindset, culture building, and long-term thinking that team ownership requires.

items.title: Winning hearts in an age of infinite travel choices
items.desc: Travelers’ discovery and booking journeys have been reshaped. How can travel players show up at every turn on the path from search to certainty?

items.title: China Auto Consumer Insights 2026: Consumers set the pace
items.desc: The 10th edition of McKinsey’s automotive consumer survey: China’s car buyers reveal where value is heading—and why the road ahead is exciting for consumers everywhere.

items.title: The CMO as impact driver: A conversation with Genentech CMO Zoë Lazarre
items.desc: Genentech’s chief marketing officer discusses AI, the future of marketing, patient trust, and why growth depends as much on culture as technology.

items.title: The playbook for seeing around geopolitical corners
items.desc: From black swans to gray rhinos, geopolitical shocks are multiplying. Here’s the tool kit smart leaders use to see them coming.

items.title: Medtech needs more than a market rotation to win back investors
items.desc: With industry performance plateauing, medtech leaders must earn back investor trust with fresh strategies and better execution.

items.desc: From shipping and rare earths to energy and security, the Arctic is gaining importance in the global economy. The Financial Times’ Rana Foroohar explores its role in a new era of great-power competition.

items.title: Using production rates to excel at executing construction projects

items.desc: Boards and CEOs can build value-creation plans that withstand and even benefit from shareholder activist scrutiny.
